added_claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
added_claims.quote: it it it gets so much tension in the media
added_claims.claim: The 200-day moving average gets heavy media attention, so crossing it works as a widely watched focal point that signals something fundamental has changed and can itself shift behaviour.
added_claims.conditions: self-fulfilling effect depends on the average being widely followed
added_claims.testable: partly - hard to separate attention effect from information

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: people say well if I'm down you know below the 200 day moving average well maybe I got to start revising my portfolio
added_claims.claim: Holders of assets that fall below the 200-day average start to revise and sell, while others look to add to assets that are performing well, so the 200-day state drives rotation flows between markets and sectors.
added_claims.indicator: 200-day moving average by market and sector
added_claims.direction: sell markets below the 200-day; add to markets that remain above it
added_claims.testable: partly - cross-market 200-day state vs subsequent flows

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: you can almost think of it in a mortality table
added_claims.claim: Expansions can be viewed with a mortality-table analogy: as an expansion ages there are more chances for something to go wrong with its economic health, so the hazard of it ending rises with age even though the cause is usually an error.
added_claims.indicator: age of expansion / hazard of recession
added_claims.testable: partly - duration dependence of expansions is testable

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: the amount of time that we spend in recession is less
added_claims.claim: Since World War II recoveries have lasted longer and less time is spent in recession than before, which Mark attributes to fewer forced policy errors.
added_claims.indicator: length of expansions and recessions pre- vs post-WWII

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: just because we've made fewer fewer errors in the past doesn't mean that we won't make errors in the future
added_claims.claim: Fewer policy errors historically does not rule out future ones; the relevant unforced error today is an uncertainty shock, which can end a recovery.
added_claims.testable: no - judgement about future policy errors

added_claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
added_claims.quote: you've got uncertainty around the actual action and you've got uncertainty around the impact of the action
added_claims.claim: Policy uncertainty has stacked layers: erratic action (tariffs on, off, delayed), disputed economic impact of policies not used for a long time, and unknown central-bank reaction, so uncertainty is compounded.

added_claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
added_claims.quote: higher risk premium you know mechanically should mean future earnings are discounted at a higher rate
added_claims.claim: A higher required risk premium mechanically raises the discount rate on future earnings and so justifies lower equity prices.
added_claims.testable: partly - needs separation of premium from earnings

added_claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
added_claims.quote: Does it matter? It's a trend I guess is is what trend followers would say.
added_claims.claim: In Q1 2025 bonds were range-bound with some flight to quality and gold was the standout trend; a trend follower does not need to know whether the cause is uncertainty, geopolitics or inflation, only that the trend exists.
added_claims.testable: yes - trend rule is agnostic to cause

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: one of the key issues in uh macro finance right now is what is a safe asset
added_claims.claim: A key macro-finance question is what counts as a safe asset and whether the supply of safe assets such as T-bills is large enough; broader safe assets (not seizable, usable to hide wealth from sanctions) help explain gold demand.
added_claims.indicator: supply of safe assets (Treasury bills) vs gold demand

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: they may have periods where they do better or worse based on the regime
added_claims.claim: Risk premia and factors that work overall perform better or worse by regime, with the business cycle and inflation cycle as the simplest regimes and an uncertainty regime as a further one.
added_claims.indicator: regime-conditional factor returns (business cycle, inflation cycle, uncertainty)

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: how many high uncertainty regimes do we have
added_claims.claim: Research caveat: it is unclear how many high-policy-uncertainty regimes exist in history, so regime-conditional behaviour cannot be well tested or adapted to.
added_claims.conditions: very small sample of comparable episodes
added_claims.testable: no - too few episodes to test

added_claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
added_claims.quote: in December we had the Trump trade we had equities up we had I think gold down
added_claims.claim: The market reaction reversed: December 2024 saw the Trump trade with equities up and gold down, the opposite of the first months of 2025, which is a reason to doubt stable cross-asset relationships in a new regime.
added_claims.indicator: equities and gold, Dec 2024 vs Q1 2025

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: you might argue that this is a a time to, you know, raise rates
added_claims.claim: With inflation nearer 3% than the 2% target and household expectations above 3%, one could argue for raising rather than cutting rates, yet the Fed cut in September and December and slowed QT, so signals conflict and the reaction function is unclear.
added_claims.indicator: Fed reaction function: inflation vs 2% target, policy rate, QT pace

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: we've got higher T bill rates
added_claims.claim: Moving to safe assets is cheaper than usual in this period because T-bill rates are higher, but staying in cash forfeits the upside if uncertainty resolves positively.
added_claims.testable: partly - carry of cash vs foregone upside

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: do you want a manager with conviction?
added_claims.claim: Manager selection tension: an allocator seeing a manager for an hour tends to reward conviction over an honest curious manager who admits not having all the answers, although open-mindedness is valuable.

added_claims.speaker: Mark
added_claims.quote: I think that the prices have come down
added_claims.claim: Portable alpha and return-stacking has become more attractive because fees have fallen, the market is more competitive and alpha products are better, so for large institutions it beats handing all cash directly to a manager.
added_claims.indicator: portable alpha product cost and quality

corrections.issue: Speaker misattributed: the remark that the economy may talk itself into recession, and that uncertainty causes people to postpone investment and consumption, is Alan Dunne, not Mark.
corrections.fix: Alan Dunne: Uncertainty can talk the economy into a recession because firms postpone investment and consumers postpone spending.

completeness_estimate: 0.78 - first reader caught the main themes (200-day, risk vs uncertainty, signal-to-noise sizing, gold, trend allocation, portable alpha) but skipped mortality-table/post-WWII cycle points, uncertainty layers, regime-sample caveat, safe-asset supply and several host remarks
